problem_addressed: Joint information extraction from unstructured text: extract semantically valid (head span, relation, tail span) triples while classifying entity types. The work targets two stated limitations of existing span-/token-pair approaches: static spans formed without relational context and relation-agnostic validation that does not provide a clear basis for LLM semantic grounding.

methodology.description: RePooL is a relation-faceted text-to-graph framework with five depicted modules. It constructs a dual-view token/relation graph using subject_of, object_of, and compound_with structural relations; scores and top-K filters tokens; composes and filters candidate token-level triples using [HEAD]/[REL]/[TAIL]/[CLS] representations; updates nodes through validity-weighted aggregation; composes contiguous validated tokens into pooled multi-token spans; then performs analogous span-level triple validation. An LLM compares candidate triple sets, and its preferences are transferred through BPR pairwise alignment. At prediction, candidate triples are ranked by validity score and top-ranked triples are output; training combines prefiltering, alignment, and prediction objectives.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: The method uses a fixed task relation inventory as relation nodes and introduces three auxiliary structural relation labels (subject_of, object_of, compound_with) for graph construction and span composition. The presentation does not report use of an external ontology or ontology-discovery procedure.
